# Secrets a user cannot decrypt are only counted by `sesam status`, listed with
# --no-access or --all. `sesam show` on one names the access problem.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# bob's clone has no plaintext for the admin-only README.
rm README.md

exec sesam --identity $BOB_KEY status
! stdout 'README\.md'
stdout '1 no access'

exec sesam --identity $BOB_KEY status --no-access
stdout 'x README\.md'

exec sesam --identity $BOB_KEY status --all
stdout 'x README\.md'

! exec sesam --identity $BOB_KEY show README.md
stderr 'no access to README\.md'

# The admin can show it although it is not revealed.
exec sesam show README.md
stdout .
